# Rigid body

Query target: `RIGID_BODY`. These are static capabilities; the live session decides which objects and operations are available. See [session semantics](../data_model.md) and [write behavior](../writable.md).

Shapes describe tensor dimensions; lanes describe the tuple width, not an extra dimension. Ordering is row-major unless stated otherwise. **CPU** means host memory; **scene device** means CPU on CPU/readback scenes or CUDA on DirectGPU; **CUDA** requires CUDA. Symbolic sizes come from the live group.

## isSleeping

`u8`; units: [dimensionless](units.md#dimensionless).

| Access | Layout | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| Read | fixed, shape [objects], 1 lanes | CPU |

Current PhysX sleep state, independent of the last wake command. A link reports its owning articulation. DirectGPU disables sleeping, so emitted values are zero; omitted rows are not awake values.

## worldScale

`f32`; units: [dimensionless](units.md#dimensionless); frame: world.

| Access | Layout | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| Read | fixed, shape [objects], 3 lanes | scene device |

**Read:** requires [DirectGPU warmup](#directgpu-warmup).

The scale physics built the body's collision shapes with: the parser's signed decomposition of the body's world transform when the body was created (a replicated clone copies its source's). PhysX carries no scale. Composes with position and orientation (same physics frame) into the body's world matrix, including a character controller's: its orientation includes the capsule-axis correction and its scale keeps the controller prim's authored axes. Constant for the body's lifetime. A scale edit (a USD edit or an OVStage transform change) recreates a CPU-scene body, kinematic or dynamic, which stores the new scale; character controllers, DirectGPU bodies and kinematic bodies driven by time-sampled transforms do not apply the edit, so they keep simulating, and reporting, the creation scale until the prim is removed and re-added or the stage is reattached. DirectGPU serves it from a stored device copy, beside the pose. No point-instancer array form.

## Conditions

### DirectGPU warmup

Device-backed DirectGPU state requires a completed first step; a write never warms the simulation automatically.

### Kinematic target

Writing requires standalone kinematic bodies on CPU/readback; DirectGPU and articulation-link writes are refused. Reads fall back to current pose without a target.

### Rigid velocity

On CPU/readback, standalone kinematic velocity setters fail; other rows may already have been written. DirectGPU has different setter support.

### Wake

Wake/sleep applies to the whole articulation or standalone body. DirectGPU refuses this CPU-side command.
